company.name: Crateful
company.description: Wholesale marketplace where independent shops order from small brands, with payment terms and returns handled by the platform.

title: Crateful: the top sellers want more
brief: A handful of large brands generate a big share of Crateful's volume, and they know it. Their requests arrive through sales marked as urgent. Meanwhile operations handles disputes by email and the payment provider has sent a deprecation notice. Decide what goes into the sprint and what you will say no to.

hidden.keyInsight: Of the 28 tickets, 8 are traps and 2 critical problems are filed as minor. The best sprint delivers 861 points of value with 14 tickets, using 44 of 45 story points.
hidden.principle: Saying no is part of the job. Explain the trade-off with data and offer a smaller alternative.

stakeholders.name: Aisha
priorities: Hit the growth number promised to the board
Have something impressive to show investors

stakeholders.name: Omar
priorities: Keep the top sellers on the platform
Bring in large sellers this quarter
Never tell a seller 'we cannot do that'

stakeholders.name: Viktor
priorities: Fix what customers complain about every day

stakeholders.name: Luca
priorities: Time to pay down tech debt

stakeholders.name: Leila
priorities: More signups from the same traffic
A launch to talk about every month

stakeholders.name: Hannah
priorities: Disputes and payouts resolved on time

tickets.title: Weekly summary email
tickets.description: A short email every Monday with what happened in the account and one suggested action.

visible.impactHint: Our re-engagement emails get a 31% open rate.

hidden.explanation: A reasonable retention lever built on a channel that already works.

tickets.title: Replace the contact form with a chatbot
tickets.description: A bot could answer the common questions before they reach the team. It should deflect most tickets.

hidden.explanation: No analysis of which tickets are repetitive enough to automate. Fixing the top ticket drivers is cheaper and certain.

tickets.title: Help links in the app point to deleted articles
tickets.description: After the help centre migration, eleven in-app links lead to a 404 page.

hidden.explanation: Small value, but almost free. A good filler when one point is left.

tickets.title: Login loop on Safari since last Tuesday's release
tickets.description: Safari users are sent back to the login page after entering correct credentials. There is no workaround except switching browser.

hidden.explanation: A large group of users is locked out of the product by a regression. That is an incident, not a backlog item.

tickets.title: Scheduled items fire at the wrong hour outside UTC
tickets.description: Anything scheduled is stored without a time zone. Users in other zones get reminders and reports hours early or late.

hidden.explanation: A correctness bug in a feature people rely on, affecting everyone outside one time zone. Cheap to fix.

tickets.title: Referral programme with rewards
tickets.description: Give users credit for every friend they bring. Referrals could double our signups.

hidden.explanation: It might work, but the claim has no baseline: nobody knows how many users refer today. A share link and a week of data would tell.

tickets.title: Main menu covers the content on small phones
tickets.description: On screens narrower than 360px the menu stays open over the page. Users have to rotate the phone to reach the primary button.

hidden.explanation: Blocks a core action for a meaningful share of mobile users, and it is quick to fix.

tickets.title: Stock count occasionally goes negative
tickets.description: Two listings showed -1 in stock in the admin panel last week. No customer has complained.

hidden.explanation: Negative stock means two buyers paid for the same item. It is a race condition that gets worse with traffic and ends in refunds and chargebacks.

tickets.title: Alerting on error rates and queue depth
tickets.description: Today the team learns about incidents from customer emails. Basic alerts would cut detection time from hours to minutes.

visible.impactHint: Last incident went unnoticed for 3 hours.

hidden.explanation: Every future incident gets shorter. High leverage for a few points.

tickets.title: Remove the legacy v1 API code
tickets.description: No client has called v1 since March, but its code paths still have to be kept compiling and tested.

hidden.explanation: Tidy and safe to do, but nothing gets worse if it waits another sprint.

tickets.title: Animated 3D hero on the marketing homepage
tickets.description: An interactive 3D scene at the top of the homepage, like the ones the big brands have. It would make us look like a category leader.

hidden.explanation: High reach, zero evidence it changes signups, and it slows the page that converts visitors.

tickets.title: Password reset emails arrive more than 10 minutes late
tickets.description: Reset emails sit in a low-priority queue behind marketing sends. Users request the email several times, then write to support or give up.

hidden.explanation: A cheap fix for one of the top support drivers. Users who cannot log in do not complain for long: they leave.

tickets.title: Listing form: crop, reorder and bulk-add photos
tickets.description: Sellers upload photos one at a time and cannot reorder them. More listings are abandoned at this step than anywhere else in the form.

visible.impactHint: 38% of started listings are never published.

hidden.explanation: Supply is the marketplace. Unblocking the step where four in ten listings die raises inventory for every buyer.

tickets.title: Custom branded storefront for Castellan Foods
tickets.description: Castellan Foods, one of our top sellers, wants their own colours, banner and web address inside the marketplace.

visible.impactHint: Castellan Foods threatens to move to a competitor.

hidden.explanation: A one-off design for one seller. If storefronts matter, that is a product for all sellers, scoped and priced as such.

tickets.title: Print shipping labels from the order page
tickets.description: Sellers copy addresses into the carrier's site by hand. Typos cause lost parcels and late deliveries.

hidden.explanation: Proven in a pilot and valuable to every seller, but it is a full integration with carriers.

tickets.title: Let users choose which emails they receive
tickets.description: Today it is all or nothing. Users who find one notification noisy unsubscribe from everything, including the emails that bring them back.

hidden.explanation: Protects the re-engagement channel, but the effect is indirect and gradual. Worth doing when there is room.

tickets.title: Payout tracker for sellers
tickets.description: Sellers cannot see when their money will arrive, so they ask. The answer is always in the same internal table.

visible.impactHint: 'Where is my money?' is 22% of seller tickets.

hidden.explanation: Removes a fifth of seller tickets by showing data that already exists. High return for three points.

tickets.title: Apply the new brand colours across the whole app
tickets.description: The rebrand launched on the website last month. The app still uses the old palette on about 60 screens.

hidden.explanation: Everyone sees it and nobody behaves differently because of it. It can ride along with other UI work over time.

tickets.title: Sign in with Google
tickets.description: Signup requires creating a password and confirming an email. A one-click option would remove two steps from the top of the funnel.

hidden.explanation: Removes real friction at signup, though the size of the lift is an estimate.

tickets.title: Unsubscribe link shows a blank page in some email clients
tickets.description: A handful of recipients say the unsubscribe link does nothing in Outlook. They are still receiving our emails.

hidden.explanation: Ignoring unsubscribe requests breaks anti-spam law and gets sending domains blocklisted, which would also stop receipts and password resets.

tickets.title: Rebuild the search index nightly instead of weekly
tickets.description: Sold items stay in search results for days. Buyers click through to a page that says the item is gone.

visible.impactHint: 12% of result clicks land on a sold item.

hidden.explanation: One in eight clicks is wasted on dead inventory. A small infrastructure change fixes the whole search experience.

tickets.title: Favourites list
tickets.description: Buyers want to keep items they are considering. Today they leave tabs open or send links to themselves.

hidden.explanation: Expected by buyers and simple, though it does not change much on its own.

tickets.title: Bespoke inventory sync with Oakridge Partners's ERP
tickets.description: Oakridge Partners runs an in-house ERP and wants their stock pushed to us in their own file format every hour.

visible.impactHint: Oakridge Partners is 4% of marketplace volume.

hidden.explanation: An integration with software only one company runs. A public inventory API would serve them and everyone else.

tickets.title: Basic sales analytics for sellers
tickets.description: Sellers ask which of their listings get views and which convert. Today they only see a list of orders.

hidden.explanation: Sellers like it and some would list better because of it, but the link to sales is indirect.

tickets.title: Reviews say the reset email never arrives
tickets.description: Several recent app reviews complain that the password email never comes. It does come, but so late that people have already given up.

hidden.explanation: Same work as CRT-163 ("Password reset emails arrive more than 10 minutes late"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Serve listing images resized through a CDN
tickets.description: Listing pages load the original photos at full size. On mobile data the page takes many seconds to show.

visible.impactHint: Listing pages weigh 6 MB on mobile.

hidden.explanation: Faster pages for most of the traffic, with a standard solution.

tickets.title: Replace 'Something went wrong' with actionable errors
tickets.description: Every failure shows the same generic message. Users cannot tell whether to retry, fix their input or contact us.

hidden.explanation: Reduces confusion and some tickets, but it spreads thin across many small cases.

tickets.title: Stop the flood of payment-date emails to operations
tickets.description: The operations inbox gets dozens of emails a day from sellers asking when they will be paid. Sellers need a place to check their payout status themselves.

hidden.explanation: Same work as CRT-173 ("Payout tracker for sellers"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

midSprintEvents.title: Three of the largest accounts escalate the same blocker
midSprintEvents.description: Omar brings the same complaint from three top accounts in one week: bulk import stops at 500 rows, and each of them needs to load thousands. Two have paused their rollout until it works.

addedTicket.title: Bulk import fails above 500 rows
addedTicket.description: The import job times out on files with more than 500 rows. Process large files in batches and report progress.

visible.impactHint: Three top accounts, two rollouts on hold.

hidden.explanation: Three large accounts with the same concrete, reproducible blocker is evidence, not noise. A small fix protects a lot of revenue.

hidden.guidance: Not every escalation from sales is a trap. Several accounts with one specific, reproducible problem and a small fix is worth pulling in. Pay for it by removing the weakest item, not by overbooking.
